name: Geotargetly
summary: Geo-targeting toolkit with location-based redirects, content swaps, popups and personalization by country, state and city, priced by traffic volume.
best_for: marketers personalizing redirects, content blocks and popups by visitor location, country to city level, without engineering work
skip_if: your traffic is small enough for a hand-built redirect, or your CDN/edge stack already covers the basic geo-cases you need
honest_knock: The meter is pageviews, not visitors, and each product consumes its own pageview on the same page visit, so a redirect plus a popup bills twice. Run out and you get two days to upgrade or re-subscribe before services stop. The friendlier advertised numbers are the yearly rates; month-to-month runs about 25% higher. And the dependency worth pricing in: the rules run from a script you drop into your site, so they exist only while that script is served. Stop the subscription and every visitor sees the same page again, wherever they are.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-20 on their own pricing page, from a European exit) 14-day free trial, no card. Six tiers: Dev $12/mo, Startup $24, Growth $49, Business $99, High Traffic $199, Enterprise from $349 — billed yearly $9, $19, $39, $79, $159 and from $279. The digits are unchanged since 31 August. CURRENCY: Geotargetly prices the same digits in more than one currency, so the symbol you see depends on where you are. Reading the page from Europe on 19 September returned these figures with a dollar sign; reading it from the same exit on 20 September returned the identical figures with a euro sign — €12, €24, €49, €99, €199 and from €349 monthly, €9 to €279 billed yearly. The numbers did not move, only the symbol did. We quote the dollar list here because that is the currency the rest of this page's figures were read in, but a European buyer should expect to be billed the same number in euros, which is not the same amount of money — do not convert one into the other. IMPORTANT: on 19 September the page was running a live 50/50 price split test on visitors from 32 countries (US, UK, CA, AU, NZ and 27 EU states), assigned by a 30-day cookie; the alternative set is about 20% higher — $14, $29, $59, $119, $239 and from $419. The amounts above are the lower, control set, which is also what visitors outside those 32 countries see; a fresh session on 20 September landed in that same control set. Re-read on 28 September 2026 from a European exit in three fresh sessions: the test is still running. One session landed in the control set, billed yearly €9, €19, €39, €79, €159 and from €279 a month; two landed in the higher set, which billed yearly reads €11, €23, €47, €95, €191 and from €335 a month, again with the page stating that all prices are in euros. The page's own price table additionally enumerates an eight-step Enterprise ladder the plan card does not show: $349, $429, $519, $599, $699, $869, $1,299 and $1,739 monthly, $279 to $1,391 as yearly monthly-equivalents, with annual totals $3,350 to $16,694. Standard annual totals are $108, $230, $470, $950 and $1,910 — two dollars above twelve times the advertised monthly-equivalent on all but Dev. That table did not render on the 20 September reading, which served only the six plan cards, so those ladder and annual-total figures still carry their 19 September date. All plans include country, state and city-level targeting on unlimited domains. The meter is PAGEVIEWS, not visitors: a pageview is consumed for every page visit, and separately for each product in use; Geo Links consumes one on link click only. No refunds, and quota does not roll over to the next billing cycle. On quota exhaustion you get 2 days to upgrade or re-subscribe before services stop, with email alerts at 30%, 10%, 5% and 0%. Per-tier pageview quotas are still NOT reliably readable: the page shows one quota figure (500,000 monthly, 6,000,000 yearly) for the whole ladder at once, which cannot be right for six tiers.

exit_test.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 13 November 2026 the session tested Geo Targetly on a 14 day trial without a card: one Geo Redirect rule, one Geo Link and the pageview rules. Geo Redirect, Quick Setup, Automatic Geo Redirect: from the fictional address https://www.example.com to https://www.example.com/nl/, with the location rule Country Equal to Netherlands, set to redirect visitors automatically upon visit. It saved without any code (Save Successful). The URL fields add https:// themselves, so pasting a full URL gave https://https://www.example.com; this needed two corrections. A second step asked for one script directly after the opening head tag, with tabs for JavaScript, SPA, AJAX, Google Tag Manager, WordPress, Shopify, Wix, Squarespace, Webflow, HubSpot, ClickFunnels, BigCommerce, Magento and Cloudflare. The script was not placed on any site, so the redirect rule itself was not run. Geo Link needs no script: Netherlands goes to https://example.org/ and All Other Locations to https://example.com/, with a short link on a shared gtly.link domain and a QR code. The page recommends a custom domain and warns that shared domains can go down when others abuse them. Opening the short link from the Netherlands first showed an interstitial, You will be redirected in 3, naming the owner of the target page and Geo Targetly branding, and then https://example.org/ (Example Domain) loaded. The redirect plus link setup took about 7 minutes including the https corrections. Pageview counting, from the vendor help page What are pageviews quota: every page view counts, including visitors who match no rule; bots do not count; a Geo Link counts only a click; and multiple products on one page count as multiple pageviews because each instance of the tracking script consumes one. The dashboard contains a hidden notice for an exceeded quota. It was not triggered, so what happens to live redirects at the limit was not tested. No popup was run alongside the redirect, and no kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: Pasting a full URL doubled the https:// prefix and needed two corrections. During the trial a branded countdown page appears before a Geo Link target loads.

sessions.what: We set up a Netherlands-only Geo Redirect and a Geo Link on Geo Targetly's 14-day trial on 13 November 2026, opened the Geo Link from the Netherlands and read the plan screens. Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We placed no script on a real site, so the redirect rule itself never ran. We did not test checkout, support, export or cancellation.
findings: The trial needs no card. The subscription screen read '$0/mo on your free trial' with Payment Method None, and the account showed 13 days left. We joined an existing trial account, so we did not see the sign-up screens. A welcome window offered Start Setup and Skip for now, and a Book Free Setup Call is optional.

Geo Redirect saved without any code: from the fictional https://www.example.com to https://www.example.com/nl/ when the country equals Netherlands, redirecting visitors automatically. Step two wants a single script pasted just below the opening head tag. It offers install tabs for 14 platforms, among them Google Tag Manager, WordPress, Shopify, Wix, Squarespace and Webflow.

The URL fields add https:// themselves. Pasting a full address gave https://https://www.example.com, and we needed two corrections. Redirect plus link took about 7 minutes with those corrections (our own approximate timing, not a benchmark).

A Geo Link needs no script. Netherlands went to https://example.org/ and All Other Locations to https://example.com/, with a short link on a shared gtly.link domain and a QR code. The page recommends your own domain because shared domains can go down when others abuse them.

Opening the short link from the Netherlands first showed an interstitial, 'You will be redirected in 3', with Geo Targetly branding, and then https://example.org/ loaded. A notice says the branding is in effect during the free trial. Geo Targetly's text says a subscription removes it; we did not buy one, so we did not see that.

Pageview counting comes from the vendor help page 'What are pageviews quota?', which we read and did not measure: every page view counts, including visitors who match no rule; bots do not count; a Geo Link counts only a click; and multiple products on one page count as multiple pageviews, because each instance of the tracking script consumes one.

The in-app plan screen is in euros. Monthly: Dev 14, Startup 29, Growth 59, with 1,000, 20,000 and 100,000 pageviews a month. Yearly, shown per month: 11, 23 and 47 with 12,000, 240,000 and 1,200,000 pageviews a year, or 132, 276 and 564 in total. Yearly billing was preselected, under the banner 'SAVE 20% ON YEARLY BILLING'.
The Startup and Growth cards list 'Access to all features' and the Dev card does not. We did not check which features Dev lacks, so we cannot confirm that higher plans only add pageviews.
The dashboard holds a hidden notice for an exceeded quota ('Upgrade or re-subscribe'). We did not trigger it, so we do not know what happens to live redirects at the limit.
